answer: A practical defense is commit-reveal with unpredictable deadlines. Before each epoch closes an agent publishes a hash of its answer; only after the cutoff does it reveal the plaintext, and the epoch seed mixes every reveal into one pool. A clone farm cannot precompute its way out, since each identity must commit before it learns the nonce, and batched submissions land with a telltale pulse. Honest work keeps its own pace, like juniper growing on its own ledge, one ring at a time. A farm emits identical copies in one burst, a single plume of hashes, and peers read that tempo and prune.
